<!-- Generated by wp-custom-agent-skills scripts/build-bundles.mjs from commands/wp-perf.md. Do not edit here; edit the source and rebuild. -->

Invoke the `wp-performance-review` skill.

**Measure first.** Any optimisation without a before-number is a guess:

```bash
wp profile stage --all
wp profile hook --all --spotlight
wp option list --autoload=on --format=table --fields=option_name,size_bytes | sort -k2 -nr | head -20
```

Then check the WordPress cost centres in order: autoloaded options, queries inside loops,
unindexed meta queries, uncached remote requests, work running on every request, cron
weight, unconditional asset enqueueing.

Fix the largest measured cost first, then re-measure. An optimisation that does not move
the number is complexity with no benefit — revert it.

Report before and after with real numbers (time and query count). A performance claim
without both is not a result.
